cross_component_finding: EXPLAIN's own privilege requirement is not fixed; the page states it is 'the same privileges required to run the query being explained' - i.e. EXPLAIN dynamically inherits the credential-type/privilege-pair requirements of whatever statement it wraps (INSERT needs Write/Query Insert on the target plus Read/Query Read on any source keyspace; UPDATE needs Write/Query Update plus Read/Query Read). This is a distinct shape from every other statement page in this batch, which each have one fixed privilege per credential type - but it composes cleanly with the credential-type model rather than breaking it, since the privileges it inherits are themselves drawn from the same Basic/Advanced pair vocabulary.

notable_absence.finding: This page repeats the pattern seen on other Capella statement pages of citing per-object privileges by literal name (Write/Query Insert, Read/Query Read, Write/Query Update) rather than a single fixed row - no new anomaly here, just confirmation that the credential-type/privilege-pair model composes for meta-statements.
